Hypothesis: this gate is how the model gives non-anginal chest pain (cp:3, which has no direct edge) a lower risk: it is open for nearly every non-anginal-pain patient and almost never otherwise, and once open a higher achieved max heart rate lowers the risk further (on top of thalach's small direct -0.176 edge). annotations.hypothesis: Root: p = sigmoid(z), z = 0.323 + LINEAR CORE - 0.511*nonanginal_thalach_gate - 0.018*oldpeak_gate_without_nonanginal - 0.235*nonanginal_low_chol_gate. LINEAR CORE (16 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.779, cp:4 +0.869, sex:0 -0.760, slope:2 +0.610, oldpeak +0.559, chol +0.529, thal:7 +0.500, trestbps +0.493, slope:1 -0.488, cp:1 -0.393, sex:1 +0.347, thal:6 -0.282, cp:2 +0.273, fbs:1 -0.209, thalach -0.176, restecg:2 +0.053. Nine inputs are unused (age, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:1, exang:0, exang:1, slope:3, thal:3, thal:4; zero-effect entries of this root). Non-anginal pain (cp:3) has no direct edge; it acts only through the three children, all of which are switched by it. COMPOSITION: purely additive in the logit. The children share no hidden nodes and are coupled only through shared inputs (cp:3 feeds all three; thalach, oldpeak and chol also have direct edges). (1) nonanginal_thalach_gate: open for 97% of non-anginal-pain patients, lowers their risk, more with higher max heart rate; (2) nonanginal_low_chol_gate: open for 87% of non-anginal-pain patients (those with z-chol < 0.76), lowers their risk more the lower the cholesterol; (3) oldpeak_gate_without_nonanginal: a near-null oldpeak hinge for the other patients (readout -0.018). Together (1)+(2) give non-anginal pain an average logit shift of -0.85 and make thalach and chol slopes depend on chest-pain type. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.9381, acc 0.888 (compute_performance). Linear core alone AUC 0.934; logit SD 3.67 (core) vs 0.42 (all nonlinear readouts). Zero-ablating one child at a time: thalach gate 0.934, oldpeak gate 0.938, low-chol gate 0.938. Replacing all hidden readouts with one least-squares linear fit in their four inputs gives 0.938; an L2 logistic regression on all 26 inputs gives 0.936. Mean |SHAP| (train, all 242 rows): ca 0.161, cp:4 0.099, sex:0 0.073, slope:2 0.066, thal:7 0.054, slope:1 0.053, oldpeak 0.047, chol 0.041, trestbps 0.040, cp:3 (thalach gate copy) 0.029; unused inputs about 0.001 (estimator noise). Interpretation: logistic regression on 16 inputs plus a non-anginal-pain block whose nonlinearity is small (a linear refit loses nothing on train AUC). Counter-directional signs reported, not explained: cp:2 +0.27 and fbs:1 -0.21 in the core, the low-cholesterol protection for non-anginal pain. Compared with the 10-seed heart-s2 record (key 9083, gen 38, a different cluster of the same run): that genome has an age/heart-rate-reserve gate and oldpeak hinges and uses age; this one ignores age entirely and puts its only nonlinear effect on non-anginal chest pain.

sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: through this sum alone, compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 30% to about 2%, non-anginal chest pain to about 7% and atypical angina to about 13% (chest pain type also acts through the parts below); being a woman lowers it to about 4% and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 19%; and through this sum alone a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 36% at 118 to about 27% at 175 beats per minute (it also acts through the parts below).

sentences.label: Raising the risk

Through this sum alone, more ST depression on exercise raises it steadily from about 23% at 0 mm to about 53% at 2.8 mm, and higher cholesterol raises it steadily from about 21% at 193 mg/dL to about 48% at 308 mg/dL; both also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Rare results

parts.name: heart_disease_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: Root: p = sigmoid(z), z = 0.323 + LINEAR CORE - 0.511*nonanginal_thalach_gate - 0.018*oldpeak_gate_without_nonanginal - 0.235*nonanginal_low_chol_gate. LINEAR CORE (16 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.779, cp:4 +0.869, sex:0 -0.760, slope:2 +0.610, oldpeak +0.559, chol +0.529, thal:7 +0.500, trestbps +0.493, slope:1 -0.488, cp:1 -0.393, sex:1 +0.347, thal:6 -0.282, cp:2 +0.273, fbs:1 -0.209, thalach -0.176, restecg:2 +0.053. Nine inputs are unused (age, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:1, exang:0, exang:1, slope:3, thal:3, thal:4; zero-effect entries of this root). Non-anginal pain (cp:3) has no direct edge; it acts only through the three children, all of which are switched by it. COMPOSITION: purely additive in the logit. The children share no hidden nodes and are coupled only through shared inputs (cp:3 feeds all three; thalach, oldpeak and chol also have direct edges). (1) nonanginal_thalach_gate: open for 97% of non-anginal-pain patients, lowers their risk, more with higher max heart rate; (2) nonanginal_low_chol_gate: open for 87% of non-anginal-pain patients (those with z-chol < 0.76), lowers their risk more the lower the cholesterol; (3) oldpeak_gate_without_nonanginal: a near-null oldpeak hinge for the other patients (readout -0.018). Together (1)+(2) give non-anginal pain an average logit shift of -0.85 and make thalach and chol slopes depend on chest-pain type. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.9381, acc 0.888 (compute_performance). Linear core alone AUC 0.934; logit SD 3.67 (core) vs 0.42 (all nonlinear readouts). Zero-ablating one child at a time: thalach gate 0.934, oldpeak gate 0.938, low-chol gate 0.938. Replacing all hidden readouts with one least-squares linear fit in their four inputs gives 0.938; an L2 logistic regression on all 26 inputs gives 0.936. Mean |SHAP| (train, all 242 rows): ca 0.161, cp:4 0.099, sex:0 0.073, slope:2 0.066, thal:7 0.054, slope:1 0.053, oldpeak 0.047, chol 0.041, trestbps 0.040, cp:3 (thalach gate copy) 0.029; unused inputs about 0.001 (estimator noise). Interpretation: logistic regression on 16 inputs plus a non-anginal-pain block whose nonlinearity is small (a linear refit loses nothing on train AUC). Counter-directional signs reported, not explained: cp:2 +0.27 and fbs:1 -0.21 in the core, the low-cholesterol protection for non-anginal pain. Compared with the 10-seed heart-s2 record (key 9083, gen 38, a different cluster of the same run): that genome has an age/heart-rate-reserve gate and oldpeak hinges and uses age; this one ignores age entirely and puts its only nonlinear effect on non-anginal chest pain.

parts.name: nonanginal_thalach_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Non-anginal-pain gate (protective). 2472 = ReLU(-0.348 + 1.076*cp:3 + 0.678*thalach), read out -0.511 into the logit. Hypothesis: this gate is how the model gives non-anginal chest pain (cp:3, which has no direct edge) a lower risk: it is open for nearly every non-anginal-pain patient and almost never otherwise, and once open a higher achieved max heart rate lowers the risk further (on top of thalach's small direct -0.176 edge). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 97% of the 70 non-anginal-pain patients (closed only for z-thalach < -1.97) and 5% of the 172 others (only z-thalach > 1.53). Disease rate 20% when active vs 55% when inactive. For a non-anginal-pain patient it adds -0.684 - 0.346*z-thalach to the logit (mean -0.76). Mean |sensitivity| cp:3 0.34 > thalach 0.21. Zero-ablating its readout lowers train AUC 0.938 -> 0.934, the only nonlinear part that matters; a linear refit in (cp:3, thalach) recovers 0.938 (R2 0.87), so the gate acts almost as a cp:3 main effect plus a cp:3-specific thalach slope. Supported.

parts.original_hypothesis: ST-depression gate for patients without non-anginal pain (negligible). 2596 = ReLU(-0.688 - 0.985*cp:3 - 0.241*thalach + 0.673*oldpeak), read out -0.018. analysis.note: Ablations remove a child's readout from the logit (zero and mean ablation give the same AUC because readouts enter additively). Linear replacement = least-squares refit of the child's logit contribution on its own raw inputs. record.summary: Mostly logistic regression: 16 direct edges (logit SD 3.67; train AUC 0.934 alone) plus three additive ReLU gates (logit SD 0.42) to 0.938. All three gates are switched by non-anginal chest pain (cp:3), which has no direct edge: a protective gate ReLU(-0.35 + 1.08 cp:3 + 0.68 thalach) read out -0.51, open for 97% of non-anginal-pain patients, and a smaller low-cholesterol gate for the same patients (-0.24), plus a near-null oldpeak hinge for everyone else. Age is not used at all. Unlike the 10-seed heart-s2 record (key 9083, an age/heart-rate-reserve gate and oldpeak hinges), this genome's only nonlinear effect is a chest-pain-type-specific level and thalach/cholesterol slope.
